subject: Medinova pilot — data rights, training exclusion & subprocessor map
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medinova.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medinova.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot onboarding questions — training exclusion + subprocessors

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile. Before we move to a short pilot (3-4 weeks), Legal & Procurement asked us to confirm a few items so they can finish the purchase order: 

1) Training/use: Medinova requires that tenant data used in the pilot is not used to improve or retrain Redwood models or shared with third-party model trainers. Can you confirm Redwood will commit to a no-training (no model improvement) restriction for this pilot and capture that in the DPA?

2) Subprocessors: Please provide a current list of subprocessors (we need to check on cross-border hosting and whether any subprocessors are in jurisdictions outside the US/EU). A CSV would be ideal.

3) Transfers & residency: If data needs to traverse regions for failover, we need the SRE/ops plan and any controls (encryption-in-flight, KMS residency) documented.

I’ve attached the internal Security intake (summary) and Procurement asked for the redlined DPA back by end of week. Can you loop in the appropriate contacts on your side?

Best,
Elaine Park
Legal Counsel | Medinova Therapeutics

Attachments: Medinova_security_intake.pdf (stub), procurement_requirements.xlsx (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medinova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding questions — training exclusion + subprocessors

Hi Elaine — thanks for the concise checklist and for the timely follow-up. Looping in Marissa (AE), Ben (Legal owner for DPAs) and Connor (Security/ops) so we can answer each item and get you a redline and subprocessors CSV by EOD tomorrow.

Quick answers at a high level:
- Training: We can commit to a pilot-scoped no-training restriction (no adaptive training or model updates using tenant inputs from the Medinova pilot). Ben will confirm the precise contract language for the DPA.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach the current list. We maintain a regular subprocessors CSV and will flag which have cross-border processing.
- Transfers/ops: Connor will add the short failover/replication note, KMS options and residency choices.

We aim to return a DPA redline and the requested CSV by tomorrow EOD. If Procurement needs an example statement for the PO to tie to the pilot (e.g., explicit no-training clause + operational residency), Marissa can propose the wording.

—Karthik
Head, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: (will follow)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medinova.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding questions — training exclusion + subprocessors

Elaine — attached is a targeted DPA redline that includes:
- A pilot-specific no-training clause (Section 2.3.b): Redwood agrees not to use Medinova tenant data to improve models outside of explicit, pre-agreed experiments.
- A 30-day notification for subprocessor changes during the pilot period, and the ability to object to a new subprocessor that would cause cross-border transfers inconsistent with the DPA.
- Operational residency options and an explicit description of KMS control points for data-at-rest and in-flight.

I've also attached the current subprocessors CSV (Medinova_subprocessors_20260914.csv). It shows providers and their processing locales; the only potential cross-border concern is a managed backup provider that routes logs through a US-based aggregator if we enable cross-region replication. Connor, please confirm the default replication behavior and if we can turn replication off for Medinova.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_v2.docx (stub), Medinova_subprocessors_20260914.csv (stub), SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (stub)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding questions — training exclusion + subprocessors

Elaine / Ben / Karthik — quick ops note:

- Default behavior: pilot tenant data remains in the selected region (US-East or EU-West). We do not replicate across regions unless the customer opts in for disaster-recovery replication.
- Backups: managed backups by our partner (listed in the CSV) are encrypted-at-rest; logs are pushed to a US aggregator only when cross-region replication is enabled. For Medinova we can disable replication and restrict backups to the chosen region.
- KMS: we support both Redwood-managed keys and (for Private/Dedicated) customer-managed KMS. For the hosted pilot we can restrict keys to the customer region and document key rotation policies in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessor changes: ops will notify procurement/contact email on the DPA 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor; we will not onboard a subprocessor that results in new cross-border transfers without explicit consent during the pilot.

I'll add a short one-page operational appendix to the redline that summarizes the above; attaching draft SOC2 summary as reference (stub).

—Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medinova.com>

Date: 2026-09-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding questions — training exclusion + subprocessors

Ben / Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed appendices. A few clarifications from Legal/Procurement after we reviewed the redline:

- Can you add an explicit clause that any derived model artifacts created during the pilot will be treated as Redwood's internal performance telemetry only and will not be redistributed or used to create derivative products for other customers? We want written assurance that outputs will not be re-licensed.
- Procurement asked if we can get a PO-level statement: "Provider confirms that data used during the Medinova pilot will not be used for model improvement, will remain within the selected region, and subprocessors are limited to those listed in the attached CSV unless notified 30 days in advance." Could Redwood provide final PO-appropriate wording?

Procurement wants to move quickly and target a PO by next Wed. If we get wording and the DPA redline this week we can submit.

Regards,
Elaine

Hi Elaine — following up on Procurement's PO wording request. Below is a short, PO-ready sentence that Ben & Connor have approved for the pilot window. Please let me know if Procurement wants any different phrasing or a one-line reference to the DPA section.

PO suggested wording (copy/paste):
"Provider confirms that data collected and processed during the Medinova pilot (Deal MDV-2026-PILOT-09) will not be used to improve or retrain Provider models, will remain in the customer-selected region unless explicit written consent is provided, and subprocessors will be limited to the entities listed in \"Medinova_subprocessors_20260914.csv\" with 30 days' prior notification for changes."

If that looks good I can send a final DPA redline and sign-off checklist to procurement and we can kick off the pilot upon PO issuance. Karthik — I put the pilot start window at Sep 29 — confirm if that works.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
